candidates.name: Archaeological Museum of the Larnaka District
candidates.content: Small but interesting museum. It displays objects from Prehistoric times up to Roman times. There's also a replica of the Stele of King Sargon II (722-705 BC) of Assyria. The original is on display at Berlin Pergamon Museum.

candidates.name: Thalassa Municipal Museum
candidates.content: Municipal museum with paleontological, geological, archaeological and marine life exhibits in several spaces. One of the main pieces is the replica of the Hellenistic trade ship Kyrenia II.

candidates.name: The Church of St. Lazarus
candidates.content: An Orthodox church dating to the 9th century. It is reputedly built around the tomb of the biblical Lazarus, brother of Mary.

candidates.name: Faneromeni Church
candidates.content: This mashup of various architectural styles used to stand in the centre of the city — until 1974. There is a marble mausoleum next to it.

candidates.name: Larnaca Salt Lake
candidates.content: In winter (November to March), flocks of pink flamingos can be seen here.

candidates.name: Hala Sultan Tekke
candidates.content: The mosque is said to be the tomb of Umm Haram, the foster mother of Mohammed.

candidates.name: Ayia Napa Sculpture Park
candidates.content: On its eastern end it transitions into the Ayia Napa Park of Mediterranean Plants, Cactus and Succulents.

candidates.name: Sea Caves near Cape Greco
candidates.content: Sea Caves in a small bay. They can be reached by foot or on the road. There are also boat trips offered to the caves. The caves are beneath a cliff. They can be viewed from above. It is possible to climb into the water and explore

candidates.name: Makronissos Tombs
candidates.content: Cluster of burial chambers from Hellenistic and Roman periods at the coast.

candidates.name: Ayia Napa Monastery
candidates.content: The one cultural site worth visiting in the town, the present building dates to around 1500.

candidates.name: Nissi Beach
candidates.content: The most infamous of them all. In the height of the summer you need to get there early to reserve your patch. About 4 km from the central square. BBC Radio One has staged its beach parties here. Also Nissi Bay Beach bar features t

candidates.name: Makronissos Beach
candidates.content: Just as nice as (if not nicer than) Nissi Beach, a bit further away. At times less busy and more family orientated. In the past this has been the choice for MTVs and Kandi beach parties.

candidates.name: Dive-In Cyprus
candidates.content: A PADI 5-star dive center and Regional SDI/TDI office that specializes in dives to the Zenobia, it can also arrange nitrox and penetration dives for the technical diver. Full range of PADI, TDI, TecRec and SDI courses available.

candidates.name: Windsurf City
candidates.content: Wind surfing, foil, standup paddle boards and more. Staff are extremely friendly and lessons enjoyable.

candidates.name: @lpha Divers
candidates.content: A PADI Five Star Gold Palm Instructor Development Centre and a British Sub-Aqua Club Premier & Technical Centre.

candidates.name: Grecian bay
candidates.content: The closest sandy beach to the centre of Agia Napa, this is a beautiful beach that stretches along three coves to the east of the small fishing harbour. Not so fashionable as the two above, but just as nice a beach.

candidates.name: Vathia Gonia Beach
candidates.content: Wind protected beach. There are water sports and massage offers available.

candidates.name: Pernera Beach
candidates.content: Off the beach the "Musan" underwater gallery of sculpture by Jason deCaires Taylor can be explored while diving.

candidates.name: Katsarka Beach
candidates.content: 800 meter long beach close to the city centre with few sand.

candidates.name: Konnos Beach
candidates.content: Wind protected beach ca. 8 kilometres to the west of the centre at the border of Ayia Napa and Paralimni.

candidates.name: Aquadream Scuba Diving Academy
candidates.content: A safe and friendly dive centre in Larnaca centre. Daily dives to the Larnaca wrecks and to the best dive sites on the island.

candidates.name: Blue Pine Bar
candidates.content: Near the American Academy has a huge selection of spirits (all real which is unusual for Cyprus) and has a real atmosphere. The decor is wood and dim lighting and lots of Jack Daniels and Blues music paraphernalia. Comes alive aft

candidates.name: Caramel Club
candidates.content: Disco club. Music of all tastes from international Dj sets till morning and elegant dress code. Mixed Russian/Greek/Briton crowd

candidates.name: Savino
candidates.content: Lively rock bar with many seats and often a good crowd. Live music on occasion. Shots cost around €5.

candidates.name: Nusa Beach Bar
candidates.content: Cocktail bar on Kastella beach with outdoor seating facing the sea.

candidates.name: Edesma Cyprus Taverna - Souvlaki Place
candidates.content: Authentic Cypriot taverna, great food, service, atmosphere. The specialties of the kitchen are seasoned with white wine and home-made zivania. Direct, friendly welcome. Delicious halumi, chicken, feta salads.

candidates.name: Souvlaki.gr
candidates.content: Delicious food and staff very friendly. Massive portions. Really good souvlaki wrapped in pita. Everything is fresh and super tasty. It's usually pretty crowded there.

candidates.name: Za'atar Lebanese Bakery
candidates.content: This is a nice simple restaurant with some options on the menu. Everything is freshly made. The pizza and the falafel sandwich is delicious. Delicious freshly baked lahmajun. Delicious baked goods like baklava for around €3 (Nov 2

candidates.name: Bigbun
candidates.content: Very nice and cool place to grab a bite. Legit taste of burgers, they even have veggie ones. Crispy and golden fried potatoes were made from fresh potatoes. Interesting options. Very nice service.

candidates.name: Yummy India
candidates.content: Tasty and well spiced. Lots of options for vegetarians and non-vegetarians. Chana masala, dhal makhani and mattar paneer are delicious. The ambience is good.

candidates.name: Falafel Abu Dany
candidates.content: Delicious small veggie place on the street, with three tables outside. Buda bowl, faul, falafel salad, lovely and healthy.

candidates.name: Vlachos Taverna
candidates.content: Great local food; salads are lovely.

candidates.name: Militzis
candidates.content: A long-running favorite serving honest Cypriot fare washed down with their own wine. No points for presentation, but the food is good and the restaurant is often packed. Figure on €15-20 (April 2018) for a meal.

candidates.name: Hobo's Steak House
candidates.content: A lively cafe/restaurant popular with many Cypriots, right on the main promenade. You can't miss it, and it's often full but doesn't take telephone reservations. Food is varied from Cypriot to international cuisine.

candidates.name: Nippon
candidates.content: Expensive but renowned Japanese restaurant serving sushi. Bookings are essential, as it is packed every night. Offers a wide range of delicious maki, California rolls and teppanyaki.
